title: Lab
disabledDescription: Pass studioLab(...) from @gnldev/lab as the lab option of createStudioApp.
explainTitle: What brought this run's calls about?
explainHelp: The parts below are proposed from the run's own record. Every combination of them is played again with the model you choose, a few times each; a part's share is how much its presence changes whether the run's calls come out again. It calls a model many times, so it costs money and is written to the audit log.
confirm: {{replays}} replays with {{model}} — {{cost}}. The conversation is sent to that model's provider. No tool runs.
resultTitle: What the recorded calls ({{calls}}) depended on
notRepresentative: This recording is not what the model usually does: with every part present, the recorded calls came out again in {{pct}}% of {{n}} trials. The shares below are weak.
independent: The outcome is the same with every part and with none of them, so the shares sum to zero. Read their signs: a part that pulls one way and a part that pulls back.
footer: {{replays}} replays ({{failed}} could not run, left out) · {{model}} · {{tokens}} tokens
priceUnknown: price unknown (the model is not in the price table)
formTitle: Which parts of this agent's prompt does it need?
formHelp: Before an agent has runs of its own. Its system prompt, as written in code, is cut at blank lines; every combination of those sections is a form of the agent, tried on the scenarios below with fake tools — the agent's own tools never run. The cheapest form that passes as well as the best is the one to write into the code; nothing is changed for you.
scenariosTitle: Scenarios: {{chosen}} of {{all}} (every form runs each one)
formConfirm: {{runs}} scenario runs with {{model}}. The prompts are sent to that model's provider; the tools are fakes, nothing real runs.
bestLine: passes {{rate}} (95%: {{low}}–{{high}}) · {{cost}} per run of the scenarios
bestNote: The cheapest form that passes as well as the best one. Write these sections into the agent's code — the lab changes nothing.
sharesTitle: Each section's share of the pass rate
overlap_one: {{count}} of the other {{total}} forms has a 95% interval that reaches the best one's: the data does not tell it apart from the best. More scenarios or runs narrow the intervals.
overlap_other: {{count}} of the other {{total}} forms have a 95% interval that reaches the best one's: the data does not tell them apart from the best. More scenarios or runs narrow the intervals.
progressMostlyFailing: Most of them are failing: the provider may be limiting requests (429). Stopping now saves what is left.
throttled: The provider is limiting requests (429): waiting {{seconds}} s, then one request at a time. Wait {{attempt}} of {{max}} — after that it stops.
capsuleHelp: Change the prompt, the tools or the history, and play the run again. Every call is answered from the recording; one it never made is answered by you, or the play stops there.
capsuleToolDescriptionNew: What it does (the model reads this)
capsuleBadToolName: Name the tool, and not as one already there.
capsuleHistory: Keep the {{n}} messages before the last one (the conversation so far)
capsuleAnswersGo: {{n}} answer(s) you wrote go with it
capsuleConfirm: {{trials}} plays with {{model}}, roughly {{tokens}} tokens. The conversation is sent to that model's provider. No tool runs and nothing is written.
capsuleBadAnswer: The answer for {{call}} is not JSON.
capsulePendingHelp: No tool runs here, so these have no result. Write what the tool returns (JSON) and play again — the answer is used only in this page.
capsuleSame: {{same}} of {{n}} plays made the recorded calls again
progressRetrying: The provider did not answer ({{reason}}): the request is sent again in {{seconds}} s (attempt {{attempt}}).
keptTitle: Kept experiments ({{n}}) — every admin of the organization sees them
keptNone: None yet: a finished experiment is kept here.
keptCapsule: {{same}} of {{n}} repeated the recorded calls · changed: {{changed}}
capsuleMemory: Keep the {{n}} messages memory put in (off: would it have answered so without what it remembered?)
capsuleNoLayout: This run carries no memory layout, so where its input came from cannot be told and memory cannot be left out. Reason:
capsuleWorkingMemory: Working memory — memory put it into the system prompt. It stays behind your prompt unless memory is left out.
capsuleWorkingMemoryUnplaced: The working memory is in the system prompt somewhere the run cannot point at ({{status}}): it is shown inside the prompt and cannot be left out.
capsuleMemoryWm: Keep what memory put in — {{n}} messages and the working memory (off: would it have answered so without what it remembered?)
capsuleRecordedOnlyTitle: The run called it, the agent's config does not define it (memory's own tool, for one): offered with no description and answered from the recording.
capsuleExpect: What a right answer does (optional) — checked on every play by a program, no judge model
capsuleExpectCalls: Must call — one per line: a tool name, optionally its arguments as JSON
capsuleExpectForbidden: Must not call — tool names, comma separated
capsuleExpectAnswer: The answer must contain — one per line; alternatives separated by |
capsuleBadExpect: Must call: the arguments in “{{line}}” are not a JSON object.
capsuleExpected: {{pass}} of {{n}} plays did what a right answer does
capsuleExpectedUndetermined: {{count}} stopped at a call no one answered — not counted
capsuleExpectedUndetermined_one: {{count}} stopped at a call no one answered — not counted
capsulePathPassed: did what a right answer does: {{passed}} of {{count}}
figTimelineLabel: Turns of the thread: the first model step's input tokens, by source
figTimelineWrong: Turns {{turns}} did not do what a right answer does (✗).
figTimelineInfra: Turns {{turns}} ended before the model could be asked (hatched).
figTimelineMemory: Memory's share was largest in turn {{turn}}: {{pct}} of the input's characters.
figTimelineNone: {{count}} turns; none marked wrong or broken.
figTimelineAxis: Height: the first model step's input tokens (largest {{max}}). Colour: where the input came from.
figCharShare: ≈ character share: each source's share of the input's characters, not of its tokens.
figComposition: In turn {{turn}}, {{source}} was the largest part of the input: {{pct}} of its characters.
figCompositionNone: Turn {{turn}} carries no layout information: where its input came from cannot be told.
figShapley: Leaving out “{{part}}” helped most: its presence pulled the plays away from the right answer by {{blame}}.
figShapleyNone: No part's presence moved the plays beyond the noise band.
figShapleyLabel: Each part's pull away from the right answer (Shapley value, sign reversed)
figIndistinguishable: cannot be told apart from noise
figPullsAway: pulls away from the right answer
figForestLabel: Each arm's rate of right answers beside the turn unchanged
figForestNote: Dot and line: the rate at its worst (every undetermined play counted wrong) with its 95% interval; dashed: up to every undetermined play counted right; grey band: the turn unchanged at its best; ▲ and a square: the worst-case difference holds at the Bonferroni level. Every count is over the plays that ran; plays that failed are in no denominator.
figForestBaseOnly: Unchanged, the turn was right in {{passed}} of {{judged}} plays; no change was played.
figForestHelped: “{{arm}}” made the right answer more frequent: {{to}}, against {{from}} unchanged.
figForestNot: No change helped beyond chance; the largest, “{{arm}}”, went {{to}} against {{from}} unchanged.
figPaths: Unchanged, the most frequent way was {{path}} — {{count}} of {{n}} plays.
figPathsLabel: The ways the plays went, per arm
verdictChance: Unchanged, the turn did the right thing in {{passed}} of {{judged}} plays: the recorded failure is not representative — it was chance, and no cause is named.
verdictCause: Cause: {{arm}} — the right answer went from {{from}} unchanged to {{to}}.
verdictIndistinct: “{{a}}” and “{{b}}” both helped, and the plays cannot tell them apart.
verdictJoint: No single change helped; “{{a}}” and “{{b}}” together did ({{to}}).
verdictNotFound: No change tried made the right answer more frequent: the cause is not among the candidates.
verdictUndecided: The turn unchanged could not be judged: every play stopped at a call no one answered, or failed.
eliminationError: The elimination could not finish ({{error}}); only the absences and your hypotheses were verified.
threadFooter: {{plays}} plays ({{failed}} could not run, left out) · {{model}} · {{tokens}} tokens
threadTitle: Why did this turn go wrong?
threadHelp: Pick a turn on the timeline, write down what a right answer does, read the plan, then run. Elimination weighs the turn's parts; then each leading candidate, every absence and your own hypotheses are changed in a copy and played again beside the turn unchanged — fresh plays, never the elimination's. It calls a model many times, so it costs money and is written to the audit log.
threadExpectHelp: Required: a play is judged right or wrong against it, and without it nothing can be diagnosed.
threadOverrides: Tool results to put in place of the recorded ones (JSON list)
threadBadOverrides: Not a JSON list of { toolName, args, output }.
threadNeedsExpect: Write down what a right answer does first.
plannerLine: at most {{arms}} arms · {{n}} plays each (planned {{planned}} to see a {{d}} difference, level {{alpha}} per comparison) · at most {{plays}} plays · at most {{tokens}} tokens · {{cost}}
plannerStages: elimination {{elimination}} · verification {{verification}} · joint arm, if needed, {{joint}}
plannerUnderpowered: With {{n}} plays per arm only a difference of about {{d}} can be seen.
threadConfirm: At most {{plays}} plays with {{model}} — {{cost}}. The conversation, its memory and your hypotheses are sent to that model's provider. No tool runs; nothing is written to the thread.
reportLevel: Every difference is taken at the Bonferroni level over {{m}} comparisons (z = {{z}}).
reportShapleyNote: {{plays}} elimination plays; none of them is counted in the table above.
reportComposition: Where the turn's input came from
reportLimitTools: No tool ran: every call was answered from the recording, or by a result a person wrote (an override or an answer).
reportLimitHuman: Results a person wrote are that person's assumption about what the tool would have returned.
reportLimitNoise: Shares within ±0.08 moved between two runs of the same experiment.
reportLimitN: {{n}} plays per arm: smaller differences than about {{d}} could not be seen.
reportBounds: The verdict reads every difference at its worst for the change: the arm's undetermined plays counted wrong, the unchanged turn's right. The observed difference, over the judged plays only, is shown beside it and decides nothing.
armUntested: {{arm}}: not tested — {{n}} of {{of}} plays stopped at a call the recording never made ({{calls}}). Write those calls' answers and diagnose again.
capsuleExpectedRange: Between {{low}} and {{high}} of {{n}} plays did what a right answer does ({{lowPct}}–{{highPct}}) — {{count}} stopped at a call no one answered
capsuleExpectedJudgedOnly: Among the {{judged}} judged plays only (optimistic, blind to the ones that stopped): {{pass}} — {{pct}}
plannerWorstCase: Planned assuming {{u}} of the plays stop at a call no one answered (counted against the change): at its worst the plan sees a true difference of about {{d}} ({{clean}} if none stop).
figLegendNoLayout: no layout recorded (cannot be split by source)
figLegendInfra: ended before the model was asked
figLegendWrong: did not do what a right answer does
refusedAgentNotOffered: This run belongs to the agent '{{agent}}', which this Lab was not given (the host's lab config names its agents). Open a run of one of the Lab's agents.
refusedNoAgent: This run has no agent — a scheduler or workflow run — so the Lab has no agent definition to play it with. Open a run of one of the Lab's agents.
confirmPlays: {{plays}} plays with {{model}} · {{tokens}} · {{cost}}. The conversation is sent to that model's provider. No tool runs and no record changes.
confirmCapsuleUnchanged: {{trials}} plays with the change, {{trials}} plays as it was — a difference is only seen side by side.
spentOfPlanMost: the plan said at most {{plays}} plays, {{tokens}} tokens
noiseNote: ±: how far the share moved between the two halves of the same experiment. A share smaller than its ± cannot be trusted for its sign.
capsuleDiffNoise: The difference may be noise: its interval holds zero, so these plays cannot tell the change from chance.
capsuleDiffHelped: The difference is past chance: the change made the right answer more frequent.
capsuleDiffHurt: The difference is past chance: the change made the right answer less frequent.
capsuleDiffWorst: Undetermined plays were counted against the change (wrong with it, right without it).
noBestForm: No form passed a single scenario — there is no best form.
noBestFormNote: The scenarios or the model may be the problem, not the sections: look at what the scenarios expect and what the model answered.
figTimelineNoneUnjudged: {{count}} turns; none ended in an error. No right answer was given, so no turn was judged wrong.
verdictUntestedArms: No change could be tested: {{arms}} — most plays stopped at a call the recording never made. Write those calls' answers and diagnose again. Nothing is said about the cause.
verdictUntestedNone: No change was tested: elimination could not finish, and there was no absence or hypothesis to play. Nothing is said about the cause.
confirmFakeTools: The scenarios' tools are fakes; the agent's real tools never run.
threadConfirmMemory: The turn's memory and your hypotheses are sent too; nothing is written to the thread.
capsuleDiffMoved: The difference is past chance: the change moved the calls the model makes. Whether it is better, "what a right answer does" says.
verdictNotFoundUncorrected: No change tried made the right answer more frequent. But {{parts}} was blamed and only left out: leaving a wrong fact out does not put the right one in. Write what it should have said below and diagnose again.
threadSuggest: Let the model propose what the blamed parts should have said (each proposal is played as an arm of its own, marked “suggested”; check that it is true)
threadCorrectionsPending: Your corrections will be tried in the next diagnosis: {{parts}}.
correctionsHelp: Leaving a wrong fact out does not correct it. Write what each part should have said (JSON for a tool result). When the model proposed one, the box starts with it; change it as you like. The text stays in this page and is kept nowhere.
description_improve: Open a run or a thread: see why it behaved so, change a copy and compare it with the run as it was.
description_new: Write an agent on the page — from nothing, or copied from one in the code: its prompt, its tools and what each tool returns. Talk to it, measure it against a right answer, compare it with how it was. No tool runs.
description_scenarios: The scenario set agents are tried on.
pickAnything: Open a run or a thread in the Inspector and press “Open in Lab”.
onlyThisTurn: Only turn {{turn}} is played again; the turns after it do not change.
onlyThisRun: Only this run is played again.
expectShared: Write it once: “Why?” and “Change and try” both measure against it.
stepWhyHelp: Which parts moved the behaviour (shares), and — on a thread's turn — the suspects proven by changing a copy.
proofNeedsThread: This run is of no thread: suspects are proven on a thread's turns. The shares and “Change and try” still work.
scenariosTabHelp: Every form in the New agent tab is tried on these scenarios, with fake tools.
scenariosFromCode: This set is defined in the app's code (studioLab scenarios, or the default set); the New agent tab tries its forms on it. It is not edited here.
scenariosTryForms: Try the forms on these scenarios
scenarioTitleLabel: Keep this turn as a scenario
scenarioSaveHelp: Kept: this turn's conversation (as the model saw it), what a right answer does above, the prompt here and the tool answers you wrote. If the conversation's person is erased (GDPR), the scenario is too.
scenarioNeedsExpect: Write what a right answer does above to keep it.
savedHelp: Turns kept from Improve. They are played together against the agent as its code defines it now; every tool call is answered from the copy, no tool runs. A play's results are kept nowhere — only shown here.
savedNone: No scenario kept yet. Add a turn in Improve with “Keep as scenario”.
savedOwnedTitle: Copied from a person's conversation: erasing them erases this scenario
savedUndetermined: {{n}} plays stopped at a call the copy does not hold: {{calls}}
savedConfirmNow: Played against the agent's prompt and tools as they are now.
savedSummary: {{passed}} of {{n}} scenarios right in every play
scenariosError: The scenarios could not be played
editResultsHelp: Each recorded call's result. Changed, the scenario plays with it (JSON).
editAnswers: Answers for calls the recording never made
editAnswersHelp: A call the recording does not hold (even with other arguments) is answered from here; without one the play stops there.
pgHelp: The agent is written and tried here. Every tool call is answered from what you write; no real tool runs. The definition and the conversation are kept nowhere — unless you keep them as a scenario.
pgSystemNotFixed: {{agent}}'s prompt is built per request, so it could not be copied; it starts empty.
pgToolsHelp: Each tool's name, description (what the model sees) and parameters (a JSON Schema). Below: what it returns for which arguments.
pgOtherwise: For any other arguments (empty: the play stops there)
pgChatEmpty: No message yet. Write a user message and send it.
pgStopped: The agent called {{call}}, and nothing answers it. Write its answer and send the message again.
pgMeasureHelp: The conversation's last user message is played several times and counted against what a right answer does. Pin a definition as “A”, change it, and A and the new one are measured side by side.
pgPinned: This definition is pinned as A.
pgConfirmVsA: {{trials}} plays with the definition now, {{trials}} with A.
pgSaveHelp: The conversation (up to its last user message), what a right answer does and the tools' answers are kept as a scenario of “{{name}}”.
pgFormsTitle: Try the prompt sections of an agent in the code (every form)
pgBadName: A name starts with a letter or a digit, and holds letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' (at most 64).
pgNeedsName: Give the agent a name above first: its scenarios are kept under it.
pgOwnHelp: The conversations kept under this name. They are played together against the definition on the page now (prompt, tools, tool answers): change something and see which still go right.
pgOwnNone: No scenario kept under this name.
pgOwnRun: Play them all with this definition
pgOwnConfirm: Played against the definition on the page now; the result is kept nowhere.
wordsError: The words could not be measured: {{error}}
pruneError: The removal could not be tried: {{error}}
wordsHelp: The last user message is cut into groups of words. The model is asked again with every subset of the groups, and each group's share of the chance that the agent's next call is the tool you chose is computed. It explains one decision (the next call), not the whole run. No tool runs.
wordsGroupsHelp: Join or split the groups as you like. At most {{max}}; every group added doubles the calls.
wordsTooMany: {{n}} groups; at most {{max}}. Join some lines.
wordsPlanLogprobs: {{subsets}} subsets · {{calls}} calls (the provider gives the probability) · ≈{{tokens}} tokens · {{cost}}
wordsSampledNote: This model gives no probability for a tool call (OpenAI does not). Each subset is asked a few times and the share of tries that pick the tool is used. With few tries the shares are noisy; each share says how far chance can move it.
wordsResultLine: With the whole message '{{tool}}' is picked {{full}} of the time; with no words, {{none}}.
wordsSampledFooter: Each value is the share of {{samples}} tries. ± is chance (two standard deviations); a word whose share stays inside it cannot be told apart from chance.
wordsLogprobsFooter: The values are the provider's probability; one call per subset.
pruneTitle: Would removing this section change anything?
pruneHelp: A section with a low share in the explanation is only a candidate. Here the agent runs on new messages you write: with the full prompt twice (what two runs differ by — the noise) and without the section. The removal is harmless when it moves behaviour no more than the noise. Behaviour is the tools it calls, in order.
pruneOneSection: This run's system prompt is one section; there is no other to compare it beside.
pruneControlHelp: Pick a section you know matters. It is removed and tried too: when the check cannot tell it apart, do not trust 'harmless' either.
prunePromptsPlaceholder: It arrived broken, I want a refund.
prunePromptsHelp: Each message takes the place of the run's last one; the conversation before it stays. Write messages the agent may need this section for.
pruneToolsHelp: Tools are called in this check, but the agent's real tools never run: each call gets the answer you write here. A call to a tool with no answer gets an error back and is listed in the result.
pruneTrialsHelp: More runs, smaller noise: measured 0.24 with 5 runs, 0.10 with 45.
pruneConfirmTools: Tool calls are answered with what you wrote on the page.
pruneHarmless: Removing it moved behaviour no more than the noise: harmless on these messages.
pruneMatters: Removing it changed behaviour: this section does work on these messages.
pruneNumbers: Without the section {{removed}} apart · the same prompt twice {{noise}} (the noise)
pruneControlSeparates: Without the control section {{d}} apart: the check can tell a section that matters.
pruneControlBlind: Without the control section only {{d}} apart: the check could not tell even a section that matters. Do not trust 'harmless'; change the messages or the runs.
pruneNoControlNote: No control chosen: whether the check can tell a section that matters is not known.
pruneUnanswered: No answer was written for these calls; they got an error. What followed them is not the agent's real behaviour:
pruneDistanceNote: Apart: the distance between the full prompt's spread of tool sequences and the other's (0 = the same, 100% = nothing shared).
formToolsHelp: Each is a component too: half of the forms go without the tool (or with the added one). Every component doubles the forms.
formToolBad_name: A name is letters, digits, '_' or '-', starting with a letter or '_'.
formToolBad_taken: A tool by that name is there already.
formToolBad_parameters: The parameters must be a JSON Schema of the form { "type": "object", … }.
formToolBad_output: The answer is not valid JSON.
layoutReason_no-record: the run has no memory record.
layoutReason_no-layout: the run was recorded before memory layouts were kept.
layoutReason_unknown-version: the run's memory layout is of a version this release does not read.
layoutReason_malformed: the run's memory layout is not readable.
layoutReason_input-mismatch: the run's memory layout describes another input than the one it recorded.
layoutReason_unresolved: the run's history was too large to align when it was recorded.
layoutReason_counts-mismatch: the memory's own counts did not add up, so where its rows sit in the history is not known.
layoutReason_boundary-lost: the input processors left no recoverable copy of the turn.
layoutReason_no-messages: the run's recorded input has no messages.
untestable_memory: memory (working memory, observations, recall, recent window)
untestable_earlier-turns: earlier turns missing from the input
untestableWmPlace: its place in the system prompt is not known ('{{status}}').
untestableRows: {{n}} row(s) were removed, and no earlier turn of this thread within reach holds them.
experimentalTitle: The Lab is new: its diagnosis has been measured on 7 cases so far (4 named right), and its API may change in the next releases. See @gnldev/lab's README.
threadGuess: Guess first: the model names the 1–2 parts most likely to blame and what they should have said, and only those are played first. Borne out by the plays, elimination is not run; not, the diagnosis runs as usual.
guessVerified: Guess: {{parts}} — the plays bore it out.
guessNotBorne: Guess: {{parts}} — the plays did not bear it out; the result below is elimination's and verification's.
guessNone: The model guessed no part of this turn; the diagnosis ran as usual.
guessSkippedNote: A guess is never the result by itself: the cause was named because the change, played beside the turn unchanged, made a difference past chance. That is why elimination did not run.
eliminationSkipped: Elimination did not run: the guess was borne out by the plays.
